notes: Rock armour (riprap) around the whole island edge, built by tools/lib/shoreline-generation.mjs into the chunk records and generated/world/shoreline.json. Always-on scenery, not a switchable street-detail layer.

Every value here is an estimate for game art (production inference), read from the dated photos (Sep 2025 Street View, Commons Aug 2021 and May 2025, the reference notes named per segment), the 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial (Esri World Imagery, 0.34 m) and the USGS 3DEP 2023 DEM; none is survey data.

Segments and closures cover the island outline w26767313 end to end, by distance s_m along it (start > end runs across the outline's start, s = 0). A segment takes the OSM breakwater polygon (man_made=breakwater, material=rock) of its source_key. Its part inside the outline, from the crest to the outline, is draped on the land as a terrain overlay with no collision, overlay_bias_m above the land: the verge at the top of the riprap (the 'verge' ground cover: dry grass and dirt), with a few low cobbles set in it at the outline. land_ground stays the only support there, so route QA, the regional anchors and boundary recovery are unchanged. Two segments that meet join into one pile and one slope; a segment that meets a closure ends in a rock face.

Outside the outline a flat shoulder shoulder_m wide continues the verge's ground cover at the land edge's height and in its shading (the dirt and small stones in front of the rocks in the photos), and behind it an underlay slope runs down past the water plane (y -0.12) to toe_y_m. The DEM's gradient between dem_fit_m along each cross-section, clamped to gradient_m_per_m (the photographed 2:1 to 3:1) and smoothed over gradient_smoothing_m, sets it; relief_m of boulder-scale bumps fades in over top_blend_m behind the shoulder. Where a cross-section meets the outline again within its toe plus clamp_reach_m (the 0-9 m slit the OSM outline cuts into the north-west shore), it stops there and falls to the land on the far side. The underlay shows between the stones and stands in for them beyond their visibility range.

Stones are one shared set of fractured quarry blocks (prototypes, cycling through block, slab, long, wedge and chunky shapes): convex polyhedra with flat broken faces, sharp corners and edges, shallow creases across the big faces and chipped corners (12-20 faces; the clean block is the coarse LOD); stones under pebbles.below_m use pebbles, clean blocks without the creases and chips, each instance scaled uniformly by its size (its longest side) and dumped: resting on a broad face (posture), turned any way and tilted up to tilt_deg, then lowered where its underside would hang over the underlay. A top row just outside the outline (inner faces at least setback_m beyond it, about the player's radius), a back row piled within depth_m behind it and crest_fill stones between them make the crest one continuous low heap, as high and as dense as each segment's photos show (its crest_rise_m above the land edge for the back row, the top row at most 5 cm more, the crest fill in proportion; crest_fill_scale times the rows' fill); a few small shoulder stones in the shoulder; a heap packed over the slope to toe_extra_m past the toe, largest size class first, its small class only within small_reach_m of the outline (the upper slope the player sees close; lower down the voids stay dark); past the waterline only stones that stand clear of the water are kept; and a few low cobbles (small stones mostly buried in the dirt) inside the band within reach_m of the outline, rising at most top_m above the land, so the player walks over them. No stone spills past a capped segment end. Weathered driftwood logs lie sunk into the stone tops along the crest (d_m from the outline), and washed-up planks at the waterline. Everything is visual only; structures (piers keep the slope under them, slipways cut it) clear the stones by clearance_m, except stones that top out under_drop_m below the land edge under a pier, paths clear the cobbles, and the street-detail hard shapes (spawn, ferry path, QA route, stairs, doors, approaches) clear everything. Stones are batched per section_m of shore, band and shape; each batch fades out over its visibility_m [end, margin] (pebble: the small clean stones of the top and heap bands).

Closures: kind wall is a concrete face under the land edge (coping_m above it) down to wall_bottom_y_m, for pier and platform edges the photos show as vertical; kind ramp is a boat ramp, a slab running out from the land edge at ramp_grade to ramp_bottom_y_m between side walls ramp_wall_m high; kind none builds nothing (the causeway's Yerba Buena context terrain, or the inlet the next segment's clamped slope fills).

segments.reason: The north-west shore below the Gateview and Bayside housing, from the small concrete structure at the north-west corner past the island's westernmost point to the tip of the sliver the OSM outline splits off the shore; runs across the outline's start (s = 0).
segments.reference: Street View contributor panoramas, May 2024 (John Ewing, from the shore path; refs/sv 01 s4800, 02 s5100, 03 s0, 04 s150, 05 s700, 26 s4708): a continuous crest of dumped angular grey and grey-tan stone 0.4-1.2 m, 0.3-0.8 m above a dry-grass or gravel verge, barely above the grass at s0; the 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial tiles t4750, t5000, t0000 and t0250 show the band with surf at its foot

segments.reason: The west shore from the head of the OSM slit (its clamped slope fills the slit) past Cityside Park and the ferry plaza to the causeway, the first shore a ferry arrival sees; contains the step 1b pilot (s 1380-1740).
segments.reference: Cityside: Street View official Jan 2023 (refs/sv 06, before the park: a low crest of mixed brown and grey stone 0.5-1 m above a bare strip, water right behind) and a contributor place photo of Sep 2025 (Cityside refs ph01: a planted crest running up to dark angular riprap); ferry plaza: ferry-shelter refs, Sep 2025 Street View 12-sv-road-sw-zoom (83 Treasure Island Rd), Sep 2026 29-sv-water-ne from the float, Commons c01 and c08 (Aug 2021) and c10 (May 2025); 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial tiles t0250-t1750; USGS 3DEP 2023 profiles: crest 3.2-3.9 m NAVD88, 2:1 to 3:1 to the water

segments.reason: The causeway's east flank and the south shore along the Treasure Island Yacht Harbor in Clipper Cove, to the small concrete pier w1222505174.
segments.reference: 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial tiles t1750 and t2000: dark stone along the marina's landward edge, the docks' gangways landing on it; Street View official Mar 2025 (refs/sv 07, s1840) shows the causeway's east flank as a vegetated slope down to the marina, its foot hidden, and official Nov 2025 (09, s1950) only construction fencing: the stone follows the OSM tag (known gap)

segments.reason: The south shore east of the yacht harbor, to the Sailing Center's small piers.
segments.reference: Street View contributor panoramas Aug 2017 (refs/sv 10) and May 2019 (11, s2230): riprap of grey-tan angular stones 0.3-0.8 m with a low crest down into the calm water of Clipper Cove and a green algae band about 0.5 m deep at the waterline; 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial tile t2250

segments.reason: The short stretch of stone between the Sailing Center's small piers and its boat ramp.
segments.reference: 2026-05-26 Vantor aerial plots a02-clipper-east and a06-sailing-ramp; no dated ground view of this stretch (known gap): the stone follows the OSM tag

segments.reason: The south-east shore from the Sailing Center platform north to Pier 1.
